newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended slightly higher on Monday as the market shrugged off U.S. economic figures which were considered negative for debt markets.
"There's an enormous underlying strength, given the market did not slip on these figures. Apparently, market players bet on bonds to continue their way upward," one dealer said.

The February National Association of Purchasing Management in the U.S. showed the prices paid index rose to 55.1 in February from 51.4 in January, while the overall NAPM index climbed to 53.1 from 52.0.
Bond trade remained thin throughout the day.
Dealers said most trade was done in paper maturing after 2006, with professional players doing most of the business.
"End-investors are wary of the current high levels, but they'll be back once they realise yields won't rise shortly," said one dealer who anticipated a further rise in bond prices.
He said he expected the Bund future to rise to around 105.50 before a turning around.
"At those levels, we'll start to put additional guards on the dikes. We'll shorten positions, focus on the most liduid issues and cover ourselves with futures," he said.
"But before that, there's some way up to go."
